problem_statement: Tidepool Supply Co. is a static multi-page coastal-apparel shop (ThePratham28 E-Commerce-Website-Template) with a home page (index.html), a shop grid (shop.html), a product detail page (sproduct.html), a cart page (cart.html), plus Blog, About and Contact pages, local product imagery, a mint/teal Spartan theme, and a mobile nav toggle. The header on every page carries the brand logo, nav and a cart icon with a 'Bag (N)' readout (#bagCount), and the home and shop pages carry a 'Bag readiness' chip strip (.bag-prep) beneath the product grid. Complete and repair the cross-page bag experience so it is consistent, responsive, visually on-brand and actually wired: (a) add a shared 'Your bag' summary bar (.bag-bar) to the header of EVERY commerce page (home, shop AND cart) so the bag summary is reachable site-wide, styled in the Tidepool mint/teal look; (b) keep the 'Bag readiness' chip row from overflowing the 390px mobile viewport on the home and shop pages — let the chips wrap / use a fluid row instead of a fixed-width non-wrapping row, and do not merely clip it with overflow-x:hidden; (c) keep the readiness strip and bag bar visually faithful to the reference Tidepool palette (pale-green #e3f6f5 surface, teal #088178 accent), not a collapsed off-palette restyle; and (d) wire each product card's 'Add to bag' button so that clicking it increments the shared 'Bag (N)' readout next to the navbar cart icon, not merely highlight the button. Preserve the Tidepool identity, navigation, footer, local product imagery, and the desktop/tablet layout.
required_content: Add a shared 'Your bag' bag bar (class 'bag-bar', containing the text 'Your bag') to the header area of ALL THREE commerce pages (index.html, shop.html, cart.html) so the bag summary appears consistently site-wide, not only on some pages.

Keep the 'Bag readiness' chip row (.bag-prep-row) responsive so the mobile home page and mobile shop page have NO horizontal overflow at 390px (wrap the chips / fluid row). Do not clip the overflow with overflow-x:hidden; the document itself must not exceed the mobile viewport width.
Keep the desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts free of horizontal overflow.

Style the readiness strip and the bag bar to match the reference Tidepool look (pale-green #e3f6f5 surface, teal #088178 accent) — the rendered strip/bar must be visually faithful to the reference, not a collapsed or off-palette (dark/charcoal) restyle.

Wire each product card's 'Add to bag' button (class 'add-to-cart') so that clicking it increments the shared readout '#bagCount' to 'Bag (1)', 'Bag (2)', ... (next to the navbar cart icon), in addition to highlighting the clicked button — the post-click terminal state must reflect the added item, not stay at 'Bag (0)'.
Do not damage the existing Tidepool branding, navigation (Home / Shop / Cart), hero, product grids, footer, contact details, or local product imagery on any page.
design_constraints: Treat the work as focused feature completion + a responsive/visual repair inside the existing static HTML/CSS/JS architecture, not a redesign or a new page.
Use the existing mint/teal Tidepool visual language (#088178 accents, pale-green #e3f6f5 / #cce7e5 surfaces, Spartan typography) already used by the strip and bar.
Do not remove the readiness strip, the shared bag bar, the add-to-cart buttons, the #bagCount readout, the nav, product grids, or footer.
Do not add dependencies, remote APIs, remote images, remote fonts, generated output files, backend code, or a replacement layout framework; work inside the existing static CSS/JS.
The readiness chip row and the bag bar must fit within 1440px desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile viewports without horizontal overflow, and must render in the Tidepool mint/teal palette.
state_constraints: desktop_home / tablet_home / mobile_home verify the home shell, local imagery, navigation, the shared bag bar, the bag-readiness strip, footer and responsive layout.
desktop_bagprep / mobile_bagprep scroll the 'Bag readiness' strip into view to verify it renders in the Tidepool palette and reflows without horizontal overflow on mobile.
desktop_shop / mobile_shop verify the shop grid, the shared bag bar and the readiness strip render and reflow without overflow at 390px.
desktop_product verifies the product detail page keeps its gallery, size select and Add To Cart control.
desktop_add_to_cart clicks a product card's 'Add to bag' button and verifies the shared 'Bag (N)' readout increments to 'Bag (1)'.
desktop_cart verifies the shared 'Your bag' bar is also present on the cart page (cross-page consistency).

change_completion: The shared 'Your bag' bar appears in the header of all three commerce pages (home, shop, cart).
Clicking a product card's 'Add to bag' button increments the shared '#bagCount' readout to 'Bag (1)'.
design_consistency: The readiness strip and bag bar keep the Tidepool mint/teal palette (#e3f6f5 surface, #088178 accent) and are visually faithful to the reference.
The same bag-bar component is consistent across all three pages; the hero, product grids, and footer remain visually recognizable.
responsive: The home and shop pages have no horizontal overflow on the 390px mobile states.
Desktop and tablet states remain free of horizontal overflow.
regression: Home, shop, product and cart pages retain their original Tidepool branding, nav labels, and local imagery.
No new dependency, remote asset, generated build artifact, or broad redesign is introduced.

author_notes: L4 experience-continuity harden on a real static commerce shop (Tidepool Supply Co.). The graded surface is a single stylesheet (css/bag-continuity.css) plus a single script (bag-continuity.js) plus the shared 'Your bag' bar placement across index.html, shop.html and cart.html. Four orthogonal discriminators: D6 no_horizontal_overflow on the bag-readiness chip row; D2 cross-page dom_assertions on the shared bag bar (baseline ships it nowhere, bad forgets the cart page); D3 visual_regression on the bag-readiness strip (bad's collapsed charcoal off-palette restyle fails pixelmatch/ssim/block_fidelity while text stays correct); D4 interaction_assertions on the add-to-cart wiring (bad highlights the button but leaves the shared 'Bag (N)' readout stale). Content and DOM are byte-identical across all three legs except the graded stylesheet, the graded script and the bag-bar presence. Local Tidepool product imagery and the mint/teal Spartan theme are reused throughout; no remote or placeholder media is introduced.
